why_committed: Unblocks I-2's redraft with trunk numbers only. Two attempts recorded because the RUNBOOK's literal command (no --node-options) does not survive this geometry -- premise drift discovered while executing, same class the RUNBOOK's own rot warning names for the version premise.
zotero: Zotero 10.0 local API on 127.0.0.1:23119, real personal library (7 541 top-level items, 5 999 with attempted fulltext extraction, 477 512 passages / 465 110 fulltext passages at completion)

attempt_1_default_heap.outcome: CRASHED -- FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory, at 190 s wall (GC log timestamp), after the last recorded poll at 177 s. No RESULT line: run_build.py's own vmhwm_kb() then raised (the server pid was gone, /proc/<pid>/status had no VmHWM line), so run_build.py itself also raised rather than reporting a fabricated peak -- the RuntimeError in the log is that guard, not a second defect.
attempt_1_default_heap.source_log: local to the run, NOT committed -- *.log.txt is gitignored repo-wide (commit 7d4db23); crash context quoted directly in outcome/last_observed_progress above
attempt_1_default_heap.note: The RUNBOOK's step 4b command carries no --node-options. This is the literal command as written, and it does not complete at this geometry -- a driver/backend gap the RUNBOOK did not flag, distinct from the version-premise gap it did flag. Not fixed in run_build.py itself (the flag already exists and is documented in the driver's own --node-options help text); the fix is supplying it at the call site, done in attempt 2.

attempt_2_heap_10gb.why_10gb: Matches the order of magnitude already used for this backend at this geometry in bench/results/json-baseline/SUMMARY.json (12288 MiB, a prior, pre-v1.10.0 session establishing that the memory/JSON backend cannot persist the full uncapped-chars library at all -- rung 'rall-nochar' there reached only 6 100/7 541 items before persist_failed with a 12 GiB heap). 10 GiB was chosen to fit this machine's headroom at run time (free -m: ~12.5 GiB available, swap already saturated) while remaining in the same range as that precedent.
attempt_2_heap_10gb.outcome: The in-memory build COMPLETED in full -- reached the full real geometry (477 512 passages, 465 110 fulltext passages, 5 999/5 999 fulltext items scanned, matching bench/results/0011-rss's 477 512/465 110 class exactly) -- but PERSISTING it to disk did not: repeated 'WARN Could not persist index: Invalid string length' from item ~5100 onward, and the final status carries persistError: 'Invalid string length'. This is a V8 single-string-length ceiling hit by JSON.stringify()-ing the whole in-memory index, not a heap-size question -- more heap could not fix it, since the failure is a maximum-string-length limit, not an allocation failure. It confirms and sharpens the earlier json-baseline finding (which called it 'persist_failed' without naming the mechanism): the memory/JSON backend structurally cannot serialize a real-scale uncapped-chars index to a single JSON file, on trunk v1.10.0, independent of heap size.
attempt_2_heap_10gb.files_note: The 486,5 MiB search-index.json on disk is a STALE PARTIAL checkpoint from an earlier successful persist attempt before the string-length limit was hit (the build persists incrementally as it grows) -- it is NOT the completed 477 512-passage index, which was never written. Do not query against this data dir as if it holds the full index.
attempt_2_heap_10gb.source_log: local to the run, NOT committed -- *.log.txt is gitignored repo-wide (commit 7d4db23); the RESULT line and persist warnings are quoted directly in outcome/status/files above

the_wall_time_answer: 270,8 s to complete the in-memory scan/index of the full uncapped real library on trunk v1.10.0's memory backend (peak RSS 8 130,7 MiB with a 10 GiB heap) -- but this is a wall time for an index that is built and unusable, not shipped: it cannot be persisted at this geometry, on this backend, regardless of heap. The comparable SQLITE figure for the same uncapped geometry is bench/results/0011-rss/uncapped-build-3.json (371,6 s, 1 848,8 MiB peak, persists fine to a 949,4 MiB .sqlite file) -- SQLite is both faster to reach a usable state and the only backend that reaches one at this geometry.
